body:
## Goal
Provide a dependency-free Node.js HTTP server that answers GET / with an HTML Hello, World! response so the project has a runnable entry point.

## Spec
Implement the server with Node's built-in `node:http` module only — no Express or other web framework, no npm runtime dependencies. Server binds to `process.env.PORT` parsed as an integer, defaulting to 3000 when PORT is unset or empty. A GET request to path `/` MUST respond `200` with header `Content-Type: text/html` (charset suffix permitted) and a body containing the exact substring `Hello, World!`. package.json already declares `"type": "module"`; add a `"start"` script that launches the server via `node <entry>`. Keep the runtime surface to one source file plus the existing package.json; other paths/methods MAY return 404 but that is not required by acceptance.

## Changes
- `server.js` — creates
- `package.json` — refactors-existing

## Acceptance
- [ ] AC-1: package.json defines a "start" script that runs the single server source file with node (the existing "type": "module" declaration is preserved)
- [ ] AC-2: The server source file imports only Node built-in modules (node:http) and declares no external web framework dependency
- [ ] AC-3: With PORT unset the server listens on port 3000; when PORT is set the server listens on that port
- [ ] AC-4: A GET request to / returns HTTP status 200 with a Content-Type header of text/html and a body containing the exact text "Hello, World!"

## Verify
- PORT=3100 node server.js & pid=$!; sleep 1; curl -si http://localhost:3100/ | tee /tmp/hw.txt; kill $pid; grep -q '^HTTP/1.1 200' /tmp/hw.txt && grep -qi '^Content-Type: text/html' /tmp/hw.txt && grep -q 'Hello, World!' /tmp/hw.txt (e2e)
- node --check server.js (validate)

## Non-Goals
- Routing framework or middleware layer
- TLS/HTTPS termination
- Static file serving or templating beyond the single Hello, World! response
- Persistence, logging infrastructure, or configuration beyond PORT
